subject: Packaging options workshop — scenario review & amendment/rollback ask
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Ava Brooks <ava@novamed.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options workshop — proposed scenarios + ask

Hi Ava / procurement team,

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. As promised, I pulled together three packaging scenarios for the workshop next week (attached):

1) Conservative pilot (Compact): minimal feature set, metered usage, no reserved capacity. Low commitment, low initial price. Good if you want to validate outputs first.

2) Throughput-first pilot (Reserved + Burst): dedicated capacity with burst pools, higher throughput/shorter latency. Includes prefix caching and optional KV cache. Works well for high-volume inference.

3) Feature-rich (Tier Plus): full feature access (advanced routing, extended retention, premium support), modest reserved capacity. Best for active productization.

Quick asks:
- Please review the attached spreadsheet and mark the scenario you prefer (A / B / C) by EOD Mon.
- Can you confirm whether procurement will require a 30/60/90-day cancellation window in the amendment?
- We recommend a canary rollout (48–72 hour window) with an explicit rollback credit if the canary triggers a regression — is that acceptable?

I’ve attached the spreadsheet with scenario-level pricing and a starter amendment draft (pricing cells highlighted). If helpful, Ben and Kimberly can join the workshop to walk through tradeoffs.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Packaging, Redwood Inference
[hannah@redwood.com]

Attachment: packaging-scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet, 4 sheets)
From: Ava Brooks <ava@novamed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 10:12:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options workshop — proposed scenarios + ask

Hannah —

Thanks for the clear options. A couple of quick points from our side:

- Pricing delta: can you put the delta between Compact and Throughput-first in absolute monthly $ terms (not just %)? Helps us with internal budgeting.
- Pilot seat cap: for the pilot period we’d like to cap seats at 25% of production expected to limit spend during evaluation. Can you reflect that as a configurable cap in the amendment?
- Rollback credit: procurement will need language that the credit is applied automatically if the rollback is executed due to measurable regression. We can share suggested wording.

Looping in procurement so they can flag contract constraints. Will aim to choose Scenario A/B/C by Tue EOD.

Thanks,
Ava Brooks
Director, AI Platform — Novamed
ava@novamed.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Brooks <ava@novamed.com>, Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 14:40:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options workshop — proposed scenarios + ask

Nice, thanks Hannah. A few price/structure notes from pricing:

- Absolute deltas (ballpark monthly): Compact -> $12k/mo, Throughput-first -> $28k/mo, Tier Plus -> $42k/mo (these are illustrative; spreadsheet has line items).
- Concession proposal: 10% list discount if Novamed signs a 12-month commitment on the Throughput-first package. Alternatively, 5% for a 6-month term. Discount applies to base monthly and is not retroactive for overage charges.
- Tradeoffs: to make the 10% attractive, we ask for flexibility on burst allocation (we reserve right to gate burst if abuse patterns surface).

Kimberly — can you confirm the technical rollback SLAs (metrics window, detection thresholds) so we can bake that into amendment-draft.pdf? I attached an internal version; Hannah, please confirm if we can share the updated draft with Novamed tomorrow.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: amendment-draft.pdf (redlined contract excerpt)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Ava Brooks <ava@novamed.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:22:55 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options workshop — proposed scenarios + ask

Hi all —

Technical confirmation and suggested rollback language:

- Canary window: we propose a 48-hour canary window for traffic routed to the new package. Monitoring will evaluate latency P95, token error rates, and output-quality regressions against a small prompt set.
- Trigger thresholds: auto-rollback if latency P95 increases >25% AND error rate increases >0.5% versus baseline for the window.
- Credit model: if an auto-rollback occurs due to a regression as defined above, Novamed will receive a credit equal to 10% of that month’s base invoice. The credit applies after engineering triage confirms the regression (troubleshooting window up to 72 hours).

Options to soften impact: we can gate advanced features (e.g., streaming, function-calls) behind a feature-flag during canary. That reduces blast radius and might avoid rollback altogether.

Hannah — I updated amendment-draft.pdf with these sections and highlighted the SLA/credit language. Ben — if pricing is agreed, we can circulate this to procurement as the basis for a short amendment.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Inference Reliability — Redwood Inference

Attachment: amendment-draft.pdf (updated with SLA & rollback language)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Ava Brooks <ava@novamed.com>, Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 15:05:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options workshop — scenario review & amendment/rollback ask

Ava / procurement team — thanks for the quick review and useful questions. Summary and next steps: 

1) Novamed preference: please confirm scenario choice by Tue 7/6. We’ve penciled in the Throughput-first option as the leading candidate based on yesterday’s signals.

2) Pricing and term: Ben proposed 10% off for 12 months (Throughput-first). If you prefer a shorter pilot (6 months) we can accept 5% off. Ben, please attach the final pricing table before we send to procurement.

3) Pilot cap: we will include a configurable seat cap (25%) in the amendment as requested.

4) Rollback & credits: Kimberly’s suggested language (48-hour canary + automatic 10% credit for verified regressions) is in the attached amendment. Procurement — please review and flag any legal or billing concerns.

5) Documents & signature: I’m attaching the current amendment-draft.pdf. If procurement is comfortable, Ben will prepare a DocuSign envelope for a 12-month amendment with the 10% concession. Link will be shared tomorrow.

Action items:
- Novamed: choose scenario (A/B/C) by Tue 7/6 (Ava)
- Ben: upload final pricing table and prepare DocuSign (if 12m)
- Procurement: review amendment language and confirm seat cap mechanics

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk the amendment line-by-line during the workshop.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Packaging, Redwood Inference
